title: Fools Will Resign: Complete the Knight Fork
summary: Finish the king-and-queen fork, then check the resulting ending instead of stopping at a material count.

nodes.question: What does the knight gain by checking from f5?
nodes.explanation: Nf5+ attacks Ke7 and Qd6 together. Black must answer the check; White then captures the queen and reaches a checked winning ending after exchanges or a pawn capture.

branches.title: Source finish: trade the knight after taking the queen
commentary: Begin after ...Qd6 with Kc2, c3 and e4 retained for White and c4/f6 for Black. The earlier king hunt is outside this selected proof.
Nf5+ forks Ke7 and Qd6. The knight attacks e7 and d6 from f5.
Ke6 is the source king move. It steps next to the queen so the king can recapture after the knight takes it.
Nxd6 captures the queen. The material gain is not the end of the reasoning, because Black can capture the knight.
Kxd6 removes the knight and reaches an exact seven-piece White win: Kc2/Ra5/c3/e4 against Kd6/c4/f6. No pawn is discarded from that result.

branches.title: Independent defense: keep the knight on the board
commentary: Test a different king route and supply a representative continuation independently of the source.
Nf5+ checks while attacking the queen on d6.
Kd7 is a legal alternative to Ke6. It leaves the queen exposed to the knight fork.
Nxd6 captures the queen. All eight remaining pieces stay on the board until the next actual capture.
Kc6 is a representative king move. The complete certificate also covers every other legal defense here.
Nxc4 collects the blocked c4 pawn and reaches an exact seven-piece White win with the rook and knight both retained.

exercises.prompt: Why check the ending after Nxd6 rather than declare the game won?
exercises.answer: Black may capture the knight. The resulting rook-and-pawn ending needs its own outcome check, which confirms a White win here.

exercises.prompt: Where is the white king in the saved diagram?
exercises.answer: On c2. Its actual square and the c3/e4 and c4/f6 pawns are preserved in every verified line.
